title: NOT JUST WHAT YOU DO — BUT WHAT YOU FAIL TO DO: The Forgotten Sin That Condemns
paragraphs: NOT JUST WHAT YOU DO — BUT WHAT YOU FAIL TO DO: The Forgotten Sin That Condemns

A Christian businessman gave faithfully to his church, prayed before meals, and avoided obvious sins. But when he saw a hungry child outside his office, he walked past without helping. That night he told himself, “At least I didn’t do anything wrong.” But heaven saw differently. His omission was sin.

💭 READER QUESTION:
“Brother John, is it really sin if I don’t act? I thought sin was only about doing evil, not about failing to do good?”

📖 MAIN VERSE — James 4:17 (KJV):
“Therefore to him that knoweth to do good, and doeth it not, to him it is sin.”

🚨 This Scroll Will Reveal:
✔️ The difference between sins of commission and omission.
✔️ Why ignoring the Spirit’s leading is as dangerous as committing visible sins.
✔️ How Jesus Himself warned against the silence of omission.
THE CORE TRUTH (Greek & Hebrew Required)

📖 KEY VERSE — James 4:17 (KJV):
“Therefore to him that knoweth to do good, and doeth it not, to him it is sin.”
Greek Breakdown (New Testament Root Words):
ἁμαρτία (hamartia) — translated as sin, literally means to miss the mark, fall short of God’s standard.
ἀγαθόν (agathon) — good, meaning righteous actions aligned with God’s will, not just “morally nice.”
ποιέω (poieō) — to do, to act, to execute, showing intentional obedience, not passive belief.
📖 Meaning: If one knows (oida — to understand with certainty) what is right in God’s sight but refuses to act, that refusal itself is hamartia — sin.
Hebrew Parallels (Old Testament Roots):
חָטָא (chata’) — to sin, to miss the goal (used in Genesis 4:7).
טוֹב (tov) — good, that which God declares as pleasing and righteous.
עָשָׂה (asah) — to do, to act, to carry out.
📖 Meaning: In God’s eyes, failing to asah tov (do what is good) is no different than committing chata’ (missing the mark).

🔥 Core Truth Declared:
Sin is not only what you commit against God’s law (lying, stealing, immorality), but also what you omit when you refuse to act in love, justice, or obedience. The silence of omission becomes an agreement with darkness.
BIBLICAL & HISTORICAL PROOF
📖 Biblical Proof:

James 4:17 (KJV)
“Therefore to him that knoweth to do good, and doeth it not, to him it is sin.”
💡 Omission is sin when knowledge meets refusal.

Matthew 25:41–45 (KJV) — The Judgment of the Nations
“...For I was an hungred, and ye gave me no meat: I was thirsty, and ye gave me no drink... Inasmuch as ye did it not to one of the least of these, ye did it not to me.”
💡 Jesus condemned omission — the refusal to act in love — as a ground for eternal judgment.

Ezekiel 33:6 (KJV)
“But if the watchman see the sword come, and blow not the trumpet, and the people be not warned... his blood will I require at the watchman’s hand.”
💡 Silence in duty is sin — omission brings accountability.

Luke 10:31–32 (KJV) — The Parable of the Good Samaritan
“And by chance there came down a certain priest... and when he saw him, he passed by on the other side.”
💡 Commission = the robbers who attacked the man.
💡 Omission = the priest and Levite who refused to help. Both were condemned by the story.
📜 Early Church & Historical Witness:

Augustine (354–430 AD):
“Not only are we guilty for the evil we do, but also for the good we fail to do.”
🔗 Source: Confessions — Book II
👉 https://www.ccel.org/ccel/augustine/confessions

John Chrysostom (347–407 AD):
“Not to share our own wealth with the poor is theft from the poor and deprivation of their means of life; we do not possess our own wealth, but theirs.”
👉 Source: Homily on Lazarus and the Rich Man
👉 https://www.newadvent.org/fathers/

The Didache (1st Century AD):
“You shall not turn away from him that is in want, but shall share all things with your brother, and shall not say that anything is your own.”
👉 Source: The Didache — Early Church Manual
👉 https://www.ccel.org/ccel/schaff/anf07.ix.i.html
OLD TESTAMENT PROPHETIC CONNECTIONS

📖 Isaiah 1:17 (KJV):
“Learn to do well; seek judgment, relieve the oppressed, judge the fatherless, plead for the widow.”
💡 Refusal to act in justice is omission — Israel was judged not only for idols but for ignoring the oppressed.

📖 Proverbs 24:11–12 (KJV):
“If thou forbear to deliver them that are drawn unto death, and those that are ready to be slain; If thou sayest, Behold, we knew it not; doth not he that pondereth the heart consider it? and he that keepeth thy soul, doth not he know it?”
💡 God holds accountable those who stay silent while injustice reigns.

📖 Ezekiel 3:18 (KJV):
“When I say unto the wicked, Thou shalt surely die; and thou givest him not warning... his blood will I require at thine hand.”
💡 The prophet is guilty if he withholds warning. Omission becomes blood-guilt.

📖 Micah 6:8 (KJV):
“He hath shewed thee, O man, what is good; and what doth the Lord require of thee, but to do justly, and to love mercy, and to walk humbly with thy God?”
💡 God requires doing justice — failure is omission.
REAL-LIFE TESTIMONY (Authentic & Spirit-Forged)
⚠️ Testimony: The Pastor Who Preached, but Did Not Act

There was a pastor in the Philippines who faithfully preached every Sunday against drunkenness, adultery, and idolatry. He warned his flock of sins of commission. But when a widow in his church lost her home in a typhoon, he offered only words: “I’ll pray for you.” He never lifted a hand to help.
Months later, that widow left the church, bitter, saying: “He told us to avoid sin, but he did not help when love demanded action.”
The pastor fell into depression, realizing before God that his greatest sin was not what he committed, but what he omitted.

Years later, broken and repentant, he rebuilt his ministry with a new fire: to never ignore the cries of the needy. He confessed, “I was guilty of omission, and the Lord showed me that ignoring good was no different than committing evil.”
FINAL CHALLENGE (Soul-Striking Repentance Call)

📖 Acts 3:19 (KJV):
“Repent ye therefore, and be converted, that your sins may be blotted out, when the times of refreshing shall come from the presence of the Lord.”

⚔️ FINAL WARNING:
Many will say at the throne, “Lord, I did not kill, I did not steal, I did not commit adultery.” Yet the Judge will reply, “But you refused to feed the hungry. You walked past the broken. You stayed silent when sin triumphed. Your omission is your condemnation.”

🚨 YOUR CHOICE TONIGHT:
✔️ Repent of both sins of commission (the wrong you do) and sins of omission (the right you ignored).
❌ Or excuse yourself, delay, and stand guilty before a holy God.
🔥 Eternity will not weigh your excuses — only your surrender.
FOOL’S RESPONSE VS. WISE RESPONSE

📖 Proverbs 1:7 (KJV):
“The fear of the Lord is the beginning of knowledge: but fools despise wisdom and instruction.”

⚠️ THE FOOL’S RESPONSE (Commission + Omission):
❌ “At least I didn’t do anything bad.”
❌ “God knows my heart; He understands why I stayed silent.”
❌ “I’ll start helping, giving, or warning later—when it’s convenient.”

✅ THE WISE RESPONSE (Holy Fear + Full Obedience):
✔ “I repent for both what I’ve done wrong and what I’ve failed to do right.”
✔ “I will no longer excuse my silence; I will act in love and truth now.”
✔ “I surrender fully to Jesus, who sees not just my actions, but my omissions.”

🚨 COMMANDER’S STRIKE:
Which response will you carry into eternity—the excuse of a fool or the obedience of the wise? Heaven records your answer tonight.
WHAT IF YOU DIED TONIGHT? (Judgment Confrontation)

⏳ Imagine this:
If your heart stopped tonight and you stood before the throne—what would Heaven record?

❌ Would your book of life show empty pages of omission, moments when you knew the good to do but walked away?
❌ Would the Judge say: “Depart from me, you worker of iniquity—you saw, but you refused to act”?

📖 Hebrews 9:27 (KJV):
“And as it is appointed unto men once to die, but after this the judgment.”

🔥 Don’t gamble with your eternity.
Sins of omission and commission both condemn. Only the blood of Christ, received in full surrender, can erase them.
SATAN’S SNEAK ATTACKS (Modern Deception Exposed)
👿 SATAN’S LIES ABOUT COMMISSION AND OMISSION:

DISGUISED DECEPTION:
❌ “Sin is only what you do wrong—as long as you don’t kill or steal, you’re fine.”
🔥 Truth: Jesus condemned omission in Matthew 25 — the ones who did not act were cast away.

THE DISTRACTION TRAP:
❌ “You’re too busy to get involved. Someone else will help, someone else will warn.”
🔥 Truth: Busyness is not an excuse before a holy God. Omission by distraction still brings judgment.

THE DELAY STRATEGY:
❌ “You’ll give, serve, or speak out later—after you’re ready.”
🔥 Truth: Delay is disobedience. Satan’s favorite lie is “not today.”

THE FALSE COMFORT:
❌ “God knows your heart, so it doesn’t matter what you didn’t do.”
🔥 Truth: If your heart is surrendered, your hands will act. Faith without works is dead (James 2:17).

📖 James 4:7 (KJV):
“Submit yourselves therefore to God. Resist the devil, and he will flee from you.”
⚔️ Now that the schemes are unmasked, you cannot say, “I didn’t know.”
GOSPEL WARRIOR DECLARATION (Public Surrender Altar Call)
⚔️ 🔥 REPEAT OUT LOUD WITH HOLY FIRE: 🔥 ⚔️

“Lord Jesus, I repent of every sin I have committed and every good I have omitted.
I renounce my excuses, my delays, and my silence.
I believe Your blood cleanses me from both commission and omission.
I surrender fully to You, no longer half-hearted, no longer passive.
I choose to act, to speak, to love, and to obey.
I am a Gospel Warrior — faceless, fearless, and faithful.
From this day forward, I will not be silent.
In Jesus’ mighty name, AMEN!”
